transcript.text: Our Bosch dryer keeps stopping with the empty water container light on but the container is empty?? We've emptied it like 5 times

On a condenser or heat-pump dryer, water collects in a lower sump and is pumped up to that container; if the route is clogged or the pump/float cannot operate, the dryer stops even though the container remains empty. Most likely is fluff sludge restricting the lower filter/condenser or sump; next is a condensate pump or float-switch fault. With it switched off and unplugged, clean the door lint filter, then open the lower flap and clean the accessible condenser/heat-pump filters as the handbook permits. Do not poke tools into internal ducts. If those are clear and it still stops with an empty tank, an engineer will usually need to inspect the lower sump, condensate pump and float switch.
[Helpful to see: image "Where the condenser and water tank are" — On a condenser dryer the water container pulls out at the top and the condenser/heat exchanger sits behind a flap at the bottom front — slide it out and rinse it. Condenser/heat-pump dryers only; layout may differ.]
I've already cleaned the container filter and the condenser and fluff filters, and re-seated the container so it clicks. I can't pull the dryer out as it's stacked on the washer. What else can I try?

With the container seated properly and the filters clean, the likely fault is lower down: fluff sludge in the condensate sump, a stuck level float, or a condensate pump that is not lifting water into the container. Those need access inside/below the dryer, so they are not sensible to tackle while it is stacked. One useful clue before arranging a repair is the timing: does the warning appear straight away, or only after several minutes of drying? Straight away leans more toward the float/sensor; after several minutes leans more toward a blocked sump or failed condensate pump. If it is still stopping, avoid repeated attempts and book an engineer to inspect the condensate pump, float switch and sump drain path.
It's not straight away, it stops about 20-40 minutes into the cycle. Every cycle for the last two weeks now.

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. The most likely causes are fluff sludge in the lower sump trapping or jamming the float, or a failed/blocked condensate pump; an internal hose restriction is also possible. As the accessible filters and tank seating have already been covered, and the dryer cannot safely be moved from its stacked position, this now needs an engineer to access and clean the sump and check the condensate pump, float switch and hose. Avoid repeatedly restarting it, as the water can continue to back up inside the dryer.

Water container not seating or being detected correctly (low)
